method.patterns: bug A present = memoFind/memoEntry compare mK0[h]===M0 without >>>0 (exactly 2 comparison sites per file); fixed = mK0[h]===(M0>>>0). bug B present = exactly one dead nowin update 'd>mNoWin[h]) mNoWin[h]=d;' and one dead nolose twin; fixed = sentinel-aware '(mNoWin[h]===255||d>mNoWin[h])' style. All nine copies declare the key arrays as Uint32Array (the fixed copies repair the comparison, not the array type)
method.demo: node -e sign demo: storing an int32 with bit 31 set into Uint32Array reads back as value+2^32, so === against the original negative value is false (Int32Array compares true). This is the no-false-hit direction: a stored key can only compare equal to a non-negative operand, so a miss is the worst outcome and no wrong memo hit is possible
